title: Freezer Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The freezer thermistor has failed or is disconnected.
fullDescription:
Error 1 on a Frigidaire freezer indicates that the control board cannot read a valid temperature from the freezer thermistor. Without proper sensing, the unit cannot control the compressor cycle.

Common causes include a damaged thermistor, a loose harness, or ice encasing the sensor probe.

fixSteps.title: Defrost unit
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug freezer and let it thaw for 24 hours.

fixSteps.title: Inspect sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Locate and reseat the thermistor harness.

whenToCallPro: If the control board also needs replacement, call a technician.

faq.a: Move food to a cooler while repairing.

title: Evaporator Fan Motor Fault
shortDescription: The evaporator fan motor is not running correctly.
fullDescription:
Error 5 means the freezer control has lost RPM feedback from the evaporator fan, which circulates cold air over the evaporator coil.

Causes include a seized fan, ice buildup blocking the blade, or a failed motor.

fixSteps.title: Manual defrost
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 24 hours to clear ice.

fixSteps.title: Inspect fan
fixSteps.instruction: Remove evaporator cover and spin the fan blade.

whenToCallPro: If ice keeps forming rapidly, call a pro to check the defrost system.
videoSearchQuery: Frigidaire freezer error 5 fan motor fix

faq.q: Why did ice form on the fan?
faq.a: A defrost system fault is likely; investigate the defrost heater.

title: Defrost System Error
shortDescription: The defrost heater or timer has failed.
fullDescription:
Error 8 indicates the defrost system is not completing its cycle. The control cannot raise the evaporator temperature above freezing during the defrost period, leading to ice buildup.

The defrost heater, bimetal thermostat, or defrost sensor is usually at fault.

fixSteps.title: Test defrost heater
fixSteps.instruction: Check heater continuity with a multimeter.

fixSteps.title: Replace failed component
fixSteps.instruction: Install new heater, bimetal, or sensor as needed.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if comfortable with sealed-system work is required.

faq.a: Typically every 8-12 hours of compressor runtime.

title: High Temperature Alarm
shortDescription: Freezer temperature is above the safe threshold.
fullDescription:
HI alarms when the freezer interior has risen above roughly 23F (-5C). This may be a door-left-open event, power outage recovery, or a cooling system failure.

The alarm silences once temperature returns to setpoint.

fixSteps.title: Close door firmly
fixSteps.instruction: Check gasket and ensure door seals.

fixSteps.title: Monitor recovery
fixSteps.instruction: Allow 4-6 hours to return to setpoint.

whenToCallPro: If temperature remains high for 12+ hours with door sealed.

faq.a: Discard if thawed more than 2 hours.

title: Low Temperature Alarm
fullDescription:
LO alarms when the freezer drops far below setpoint, typically caused by a stuck relay, a faulty thermistor, or an overly cold setting.

While low temperature is safe for food, it wastes energy and may freeze items unevenly.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap in a new thermistor if reading is off.

whenToCallPro: If relays are suspected, call a pro.

faq.a: Yes, but it may suffer freezer burn.

title: Evaporator Fan Circuit Error
shortDescription: The evaporator fan circuit has a failure.
fullDescription:
SY EF (System Evaporator Fan) indicates the control board cannot verify evaporator fan operation. The fan may be disconnected, seized, or the control board has lost its sense circuit.

This code often accompanies rising freezer temperatures.

fixSteps.title: Inspect fan
fixSteps.instruction: Remove evaporator cover and check for ice or obstruction.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if sealed system repair is required.

faq.q: Can I keep using the freezer?

title: Door Open Alarm
shortDescription: Freezer door has been open too long.
fullDescription:
OP means the door has been sensed open longer than the programmed alarm threshold (usually 3 minutes).

Check for obstructions keeping the door ajar, a failed door switch, or a misaligned hinge.

fixSteps.title: Close door
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure door is fully closed and latched.

fixSteps.title: Clear obstructions
fixSteps.instruction: Rearrange items blocking the door seal.

fixSteps.title: Test door switch
fixSteps.instruction: Press and release to verify operation.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed — most cases are user-solvable.
videoSearchQuery: Frigidaire freezer OP door open alarm

title: Control Lock Engaged
fullDescription:
CL is not a fault; it indicates the child lock / control lock is enabled. Button presses are ignored to prevent accidental changes.

Hold the designated lock button for 3 seconds to disable.

fixSteps.title: Disable lock
fixSteps.instruction: Press and hold the Lock button for 3 seconds.

faq.a: Same gesture toggles on and off.

title: Sabbath Mode Active
fullDescription:
Sb indicates the freezer is in Sabbath mode — a religious observance feature that disables certain display functions and alarms.

Food safety is maintained while the unit minimizes visible activity. Exit the mode via the menu combination in the owner's manual.

fixSteps.title: Exit Sabbath
fixSteps.instruction: Follow owner's manual button sequence (commonly Lock + Alarm for 6 seconds).

faq.q: Is it safe to leave on?

title: Demo Mode Active
shortDescription: Freezer is in retail demo mode.
fullDescription:
dE signals that the freezer is running in Demo Mode. In this mode the display functions but the compressor does not run, so the unit will not actually cool.

This mode is sometimes enabled accidentally at home or left on after showroom display.

fixSteps.title: Exit demo mode
fixSteps.instruction: Hold the temperature up and down buttons simultaneously for 5 seconds.

faq.a: Likely set during retail display or by accidental button combination.
